summary.headline: Oil India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose to INR2,870 crore from INR813 crore, on record EBITDA of INR4,605 crore and crude realisation of USD98.73/bbl.
summary.overview: Standalone operating revenue hit a record INR7,958 crore and EBITDA a record INR4,605 crore, with margin above 54%. Crude output was 0.95 MMT, up 11%+ YoY, and daily output peaked at 10,921 MT on 27 June, later 11,017 MT on 3 August. Subsidiary NRL ran at 105% capacity utilisation with a GRM of USD35.95/bbl (about USD33 ex-inventory gain), and consolidated PAT was INR4,026 crore. Management guided to roughly 1 MMT crude per quarter and about 3.9–4 MMT for FY27, and gas evacuation hinges on DNPL/IGGL connectivity.

segments.name: Upstream (standalone crude and gas)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 production was 1.707 MMBoE, with crude at 0.95 MMT (+11%+ YoY) and gas up 0.4% QoQ. Gas off-take has been constrained at about 2.93 BCM by evacuation limits, and management targets 3.8 BCM next year and about 5 BCM by FY29.

segments.name: NRL (refining, material subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation was 105%, distillate yield 87%, and GRM USD35.95/bbl vs USD5.02 a year earlier. Management said about USD2 of the GRM was inventory gain, and OMC discounts under SAED were netted off.

guidance_outlook: Crude production: about 1 MMT per quarter from now on, roughly 3.9 MMT for FY27 with a possible touch of 4 MMT; FY29 target of about 4.2 MMT from main producing areas, with upside from near-field exploration.
Capex: FY27 budget is INR8,600 crore (to be revised at the next review); Q1 spend was about INR3,050 crore, including INR1,230 crore on exploratory drilling.
Wells: FY27 target of 100 wells (42 exploratory, 57 development), up from 74 in FY26; a further 10% rise is intended for FY28.

NRL: CDU/VDU, DHDT and SRU to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026, remaining units by 31 March 2027, reaching about 75% of 9 MMT rated capacity by Q4 FY28; Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline mechanical completion targeted October and commissioning by December 2026.
Gas: 200 m connection within the NRL campus (2–3 months) to link DNPL with IGGL; DFL feeder line about 20% complete; big jump in evacuation expected from Q1 FY28 and about 5 BCM by FY29.
GST on royalty: about INR2,500 crore (excluding interest) is already provided; payment to be made, with no prospective interest. The Assam land tax is a contingent liability with no P&L impact.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex about INR3,050 crore: survey INR450 crore, exploratory drilling INR1,230 crore, development drilling INR700 crore, capital equipment and projects INR350 crore, subsidiaries/JVs/overseas INR350 crore. FY26 actual capex was INR13,026 crore.
Wells drilled in Q1: 17 (7 exploratory, 10 development). Drilling history: FY25 22 exploratory and 35 development; FY26 22 exploratory and 52 development.

Andaman: Vijayapuram-1 spend about INR1,000–1,050 crore; hydro-frac testing in August; fourth Andaman well by a jack-up rig targeted for December 2026; 600 sq km of new 3D seismic to be processed by October.

Deep water (Mahanadi and KG): 4,200 line km and 5,300 sq km of 3D acquired; first deep-water rig expected June–July 2027, second by March 2028. Government reimbursement of up to INR675 crore per well is proposed under the Samudra Manthan scheme.

NRL expansion: about INR30,000 crore spent to date, with INR34,000–35,000 crore expected for the refinery project and another INR7,200–7,300 crore for the PPU project. NRL debt is about INR19,000 crore.
demand_pricing: Crude realisation was USD98.73/bbl and gas USD7.19/MMBtu; new-well gas is priced outside APM, and incremental volumes will all be new-well gas.

NRL's GRM is about USD33 excluding the roughly USD2 inventory gain. Diesel and petrol discounts to OMCs under SAED ran at INR13/l to INR3/l for petrol and INR10/l to nil for diesel during the quarter, and have reappeared as a monthly recalibration.

Gas off-take from BCPL is stable at about 1.25–1.35 MMSCMD (about 4.25 MMSCMD returned to the grid by Oil India). NEEPCO is cutting gas use in favour of hydro, and excise benefit fell as government calibrated excise to hold retail prices.
NRL operating cost is about USD4.5–5/bbl, targeted to fall to about USD3.5/bbl as expansion units stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current crude run-rate, and can production sustain the 10,921 MT/day level?
qa_highlights.answer: Director Operations said the company expects about 1 MMT per quarter from here, citing workover, well intervention and optimisation; output reached 11,017 MT/day on 3 August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for gas ramp-up from 2.93 BCM to about 5 BCM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 and H1 FY28 would be flat to slow; the big jump is expected from Q1 FY28 once the 200 m NRL link and DFL/IGGL are complete, with about 1.5 MMSCMD of extra headroom from DNPL capacity expansion and 3.5–4 MMSCMD of evacuation planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised NRL GRM, and what is the exploration capex outlook given the government support?
qa_highlights.answer: NRL GRM was about USD35 including about USD2 inventory gain (about USD33 ex-gain). Exploration: 100 wells targeted in FY27 and a 10%+ rise intended thereafter, with deep-water programme funded in part by government schemes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NRL expansion status and the Paradip–Numaligarh pipeline timing?
qa_highlights.answer: CDU/VDU mechanically complete, with three units to be commissioned by Oct–Nov 2026 and the rest by 31 March 2027; pipeline ROU is secured except about 8 km, with commissioning by December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position across the group?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone: USD1.4 bn loan for Mozambique. Singapore subsidiary: USD500 mn bond due May 2027. NRL: about INR19,000 crore. Total group debt about INR37,233 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract costs rise, and what is the GST-on-royalty payment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract cost rose by about INR146 crore QoQ to INR615 crore, mainly offshore G&G costs. About INR2,500 crore GST on royalty (excl. interest) is already provided, to be paid with no prospective interest; the Assam land tax is a contingent liability.

risks_watch: Gas evacuation remains the binding constraint: BCPL and NEEPCO off-take is seasonal and the DFL/IGGL and 200 m NRL link are still pending.
NRL's GRM is inflated by SAED-linked discounts and an inventory gain of about USD2/bbl; the normalised GRM is about USD33 and the discount level is calibrated monthly.
Andaman Vijayapuram-1 and -3 testing is still pending; a write-down or capitalised-cost review is possible after the September decision.
Assam land tax case is being withdrawn via the state legislature; the contingent liability is removed only once withdrawal is effective.
Q2 gas volumes could dip with monsoon and tea-garden seasonality from October; exploration cost (G&G) inflated opex in Q1.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on production records and NRL operations, with repeated emphasis on execution and integrated planning. Cautious and hedged on gas evacuation timelines, which management tied to pipeline completion, and some answers were given loosely or deferred. Frequent line disconnects and unclear figures in Q&A reduced precision on several numbers.
key_quotes: So at present we are on a path where you can, we can see that we are going to achieve close to 1 MMT each quarter this year.

We have always maintained that ramping up the production by itself is not a challenge. Absense of the network is a challenge which we are trying to address and once the network is laid, it is ready for evacuation, ramping up production will definitely happen.
